response.sql:
WITH grp AS (
  SELECT s.zoneregistry AS site_code,
         s.healtheval AS status,
         AVG(sc.gbsize / NULLIF(sc.spanmin, 0)) AS avg_ratio,
         COUNT(*) AS scan_count
  FROM scans sc
  JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = sc.zoneref
  WHERE sc.chronotag >= '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274'
    AND sc.chronotag <= '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797'
  GROUP BY s.zoneregistry, s.healtheval
),
stats AS (
  SELECT site_code, status, avg_ratio, scan_count,
         AVG(avg_ratio) OVER () AS mean_avg
  FROM grp
)
SELECT site_code, status, avg_ratio, scan_count,
       avg_ratio - mean_avg AS excess
FROM stats
WHERE avg_ratio > mean_avg
ORDER BY excess DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: chronotag is compared as text, as the request specifies, and its stored values share the 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff' layout so that text order matches time order.
Scans with a spanmin of 0 are treated as missing (NULLIF avoids division by zero), along with NULL gbsize or spanmin, and are excluded from the average.
scan_count counts every scan in the group, including scans whose ratio is missing.
Scans with no matching site row are dropped by the inner join, and a NULL healtheval forms its own group.

alternatives.interpretation: scan_count counts only scans with a computable ratio (non-null gbsize and non-zero spanmin), so it matches the scans that feed the average.
